steps.action: Intake verification call with client: confirm the gap facts flagged in the draft — exact date handset was handed to the service centre, job sheet/reference number, whether the warranty denial was given in writing or orally, whether any legal/demand notice was already sent, client's annual income and any protected-category status (for the free-aid re-check), and preferred forum address (residence/workplace in Bhopal).
steps.output: Completed [TO CONFIRM] checklist appended to the packet; free-aid eligibility re-assessment note for the supervising advocate

steps.action: Supervising advocate reads the junior's draft against the 2026-09-29 limitation deadline and records a go/no-go on filing route (e-Daakhil vs. physical filing at District Commission, Bhopal) and on whether a pre-filing notice is to be sent in parallel.
steps.output: Signed filing-route direction on file cover

steps.action: Client assembles and hands over documents: tax invoice dated 15 Jan 2026, warranty card, service centre job sheet, any written refusal/WhatsApp/email correspondence, ID proof, and proof of address for territorial jurisdiction. Originals shown, two photocopy sets made.
steps.output: Document bundle with index; originals returned to client, copies retained

steps.action: Verify jurisdiction and fee on record: claim value Rs 40,000 plus Rs 15,000 compensation — confirm this falls in District Commission pecuniary limit and confirm the applicable filing fee slab under the Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules as currently notified [TO CONFIRM exact fee amount and mode of payment accepted at Bhopal District Commission].

Revise the draft complaint to add the items missing from the current version: memo of parties with full addresses of Rakesh Sharma and XYZ Mobiles Service Centre, list of dates and events, prayer clause numbering, index of annexures A-1 onwards, and the statutory affidavit in support of the complaint.
steps.output: Revision-2 complaint set (complaint + memo of parties + list of dates + index + draft affidavit)

steps.action: If the advocate so directed on Day 0, issue a short pre-filing demand notice to the service centre by email and registered post, running in parallel so it does not delay filing.
steps.output: Dispatched notice copy with postal receipt / email delivery record

steps.action: Advocate settles the final complaint text, affidavit, and vakalatnama; confirms sections 2(7), 2(11) and 39 are pleaded to the facts as verified on Day 0 and that no unverified fact has crept in.
steps.output: Advocate-approved final filing set, initialled on each page

steps.action: Client signs the complaint, verification clause, vakalatnama and affidavit; affidavit sworn/notarised. Verification place and date to be filled as Bhopal and the actual signing date (replacing the [TO CONFIRM] in the draft).

Create/confirm e-Daakhil account in the client's name (mobile and email OTP with client present), scan the full set into the prescribed PDF format, upload, and pay the filing fee online. Keep a complete hard-copy set ready in case the Commission directs physical submission.
steps.output: e-Daakhil submission acknowledgement with temporary case/diary number; fee payment receipt

steps.action: Check e-Daakhil portal for scrutiny status and objections raised by the registry; note any defect (annexure legibility, affidavit format, fee shortfall, address defect).
steps.output: Scrutiny status printout; defect list if any

steps.action: Cure any scrutiny defect and re-submit the same day; if the registry insists on physical filing, lodge the hard-copy set at the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bhopal, and obtain the filing stamp. Report completion to the advocate.
steps.output: Confirmed filing with case number / stamped receipt; completion note to client

steps.action: Reserve buffer day before the limitation deadline: if filing is still not accepted, advocate prepares an application for condonation of delay under Section 69(2) with a supporting affidavit explaining the cause, to be filed together with the complaint.
steps.output: Contingency condonation application (used only if required)

critical_dates.what: Date of purchase / invoice date pleaded as start of the cause of action
Day 0 — packet date, intake verification and advocate go/no-go
Advocate settles final complaint, affidavit and vakalatnama
Client signature and notarisation of affidavit
Target filing completion / defects cured (two clear days before deadline)
Buffer day — contingency condonation application prepared if filing not yet accepted
Limitation deadline as stated in the packet — filing must be on record by this date

escalation_path: Registry raises scrutiny objection on e-Daakhil: volunteer cures and re-submits the same working day; if the defect is substantive (jurisdiction, fee slab, affidavit format), refer to the supervising advocate before re-submission.

Client documents incomplete or the handover date / written warranty denial cannot be confirmed by Day 2: volunteer escalates to the supervising advocate, who decides whether to file on available material with the gap pleaded as [TO CONFIRM] rather than miss 2026-09-29.
e-Daakhil portal outage or payment gateway failure: switch immediately to physical filing at the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bhopal, with a printed record of the failed attempt.
Filing slips past 2026-09-29 for any reason: advocate files the Section 69(2) condonation of delay application with supporting affidavit along with the complaint.
Free-aid eligibility: if the Day 0 income/category answers change the position, volunteer routes the file to the clinic's eligibility desk before fee payment on Day 5.
Post-filing adverse order: appeal route to the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under Section 41 within the prescribed period — advocate to advise separately at that stage.
Any disagreement within the review council on strategy: escalate to the supervising advocate, whose written direction on the file cover governs.
